ComparingCounter.notes: Source read at commit f6cf8d6, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.1. The counter limit parameter is configured with a default of 0 (ComparingCounter.cpp:53) although the panel letters the knob 1 and 31, and the A attenuator's default is 0 too, so a fresh module shows nothing at VALUE and nothing at A-B>T. The whole plugin is monophonic: no module in it calls getChannels, getPolyVoltage or setChannels. The VALUE output is given the cv family rather than pitch because it is a staircase count; the maker points out that its 0.166V step is a whole tone if it is used as a pitch.

DualIntegrator.notes: Source read at commit f6cf8d6, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.1. The IN inputs and OUT outputs get no family: the maker's own manual has them carrying audio, control voltage, gates or a constant, depending on the patch. The rate parameter is configured as 2 to the power of the value in Hertz, -5 to 13.5 (DualIntegrator.cpp:74), and the result is multiplied by 20 in process() to match a 20V peak-to-peak swing, so the figures at the knob are the cycling frequency rather than volts per second. The mode switch is configured with the choices Track and Hold at 0 and Sample and Hold at 1, and the maker's panel standard puts a switch ON when it is upright.

WindowGenerators.notes: Source read at commit f6cf8d6, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.1. The four time parameters are configured as 0.5 times 0.5 to the power of the value in seconds, -6 to 8 (WindowGenerators.cpp:75), so the knob runs from 32 seconds at the bottom to about 1.95ms at the top and a rising control voltage shortens the stage, which is what makes the time inputs track a volt an octave when the module is cycling. The SHAPE knob feeds each envelope back into its own time parameters, so it changes the timing as well as the curve. The whole plugin is monophonic.
